question: What flooring is best for a snowbird home that sits empty all summer?
title: Best Flooring for a Snowbird Home Left All Summer
h1: What's the Best Flooring for a Snowbird Home Sitting Empty All Summer?
description: SPC vinyl plank handles -25 F to 155 F once installed. Keep your AC at 85 F or below while away, per UF/IFAS, to protect your floors in 2026.
capsule: Rigid-core SPC vinyl plank is the safest pick for a Florida snowbird home, since some SPC lines are rated to handle temperatures from -25 F to 155 F once installed. Keep the AC running at no higher than 85 F while you're away; UF/IFAS warns that above that, indoor humidity passes 55-60% and mold can start growing.

sections.h2: Why an Empty House Is Riskier Than an Occupied One
sections.html:
UF/IFAS's guidance on closing a seasonal home is direct: leave the air conditioning running, set no higher than 85 F, because above that indoor relative humidity climbs past 55-60% and mold can begin growing. Have your humidistat calibrated before you leave; Southwest Florida HVAC companies commonly suggest a tighter target of 78-80 F with the humidistat set to 55-60%.

This is especially relevant for a house that sits closed for four to six months at a stretch, common for Sarasota and Manatee county snowbirds who split time between here and a northern home. A short two-week absence rarely causes trouble; a full off-season with nobody checking on the house is a different situation entirely. Ask a neighbor or a property manager to do a quick walk-through partway through the summer if you can, since a five-minute check can catch a failing AC unit before it becomes a flooring problem.

sections.h2: Which Flooring Handles Months Without Anyone Home
sections.html:
Rigid-core SPC vinyl plank lines are commonly rated to handle -25 F to 155 F once installed, giving a wide margin if conditions swing while you're away. WPC vinyl plank has a much narrower rated range, typically 32 F to 100 F. Hardwood is the most sensitive of the three; the National Wood Flooring Association notes wood floors perform best at 30-50% relative humidity and 60-80 F, and most flooring is manufactured at 6-9% moisture content, a tight window a closed-up house needs to actually maintain.

Laminate falls somewhere between these categories and isn't a material we'd recommend for a home that sits empty for months, since its core is more moisture-sensitive than rigid-core vinyl and it doesn't carry the same wide temperature ratings. If your existing floors are laminate, that's worth factoring into your pre-departure planning even more than the AC settings alone.

sections.h2: What We Recommend Before You Head North
sections.html:
For a lock-and-leave property, we generally default to rigid-core SPC vinyl plank over WPC or solid wood, simply because of that wider temperature tolerance. We also recommend having your humidistat calibrated as part of your pre-departure checklist, not just the thermostat, since humidity is what actually drives mold risk in a closed house.

We also point snowbird clients toward waterproof flooring generally, not just for the temperature range but because a closed house is more vulnerable to a slow, undetected leak, a supply line failure, a roof issue after a storm, going unnoticed for weeks instead of hours. That gap in risk is worth discussing honestly rather than assuming any rigid-core product handles every absence the same way.

sections.h2: If You Already Have Wood Floors
sections.html:
Keep the home within the NWFA's 30-50% relative humidity and 60-80 F range for as much of the year as your HVAC allows, and don't rely on the AC being simply on; confirm the humidistat is calibrated correctly before a long absence. If you're weighing whether to switch materials before your next trip north, a free in-home estimate can walk through the tradeoffs for your specific house.

A smart water sensor near the water heater or under sinks is a low-cost way to catch a leak early in a house nobody's checking daily, and it pairs well with whichever flooring you choose, since even the most tolerant materials do better when a problem gets caught in hours rather than months. We factor your specific closure schedule into the flooring recommendation during the estimate, since a home closed for six weeks has different needs than one closed for six months.

faqs.q: What temperature should I set my AC to before leaving for the summer?
faqs.a: UF/IFAS recommends no higher than 85 F. Southwest Florida HVAC companies commonly suggest a tighter 78-80 F with the humidistat set to 55-60% for extra margin.

faqs.q: Can mold really grow under vinyl plank if the AC is off?
faqs.a: Once indoor relative humidity passes roughly 55-60%, which UF/IFAS ties to temperatures above 85 F, conditions become favorable for mold, including under flooring where moisture can sit unnoticed.

faqs.q: Is a floating floor okay for a Florida room without AC?
faqs.a: Some rigid-core lines allow three-season, non-climate-controlled rooms, but only for floating installations, not glue-down. Check your specific product's installation guide before assuming it applies.
